1.asv: Then answered Zophar the Naamathite, and said,

2.web: “Shouldn’t the multitude of words be answered? Should a man full of talk be justified?
2.asv: Should not the multitude of words be answered? And should a man full of talk be justified?

3.web: Should your boastings make men hold their peace? When you mock, shall no man make you ashamed?
3.asv: Should thy boastings make men hold their peace? And when thou mockest, shall no man make thee ashamed?

4.web: For you say, ‘My doctrine is pure. I am clean in your eyes.’
4.asv: For thou sayest, My doctrine is pure, And I am clean in thine eyes.

5.web: But oh that God would speak, and open his lips against you,
5.asv: But oh that God would speak, And open his lips against thee,

6.web: that he would show you the secrets of wisdom! For true wisdom has two sides. Know therefore that God exacts of you less than your iniquity deserves.
6.asv: And that he would show thee the secrets of wisdom! For he is manifold in understanding. Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.

7.web: “Can you fathom the mystery of God? Or can you probe the limits of the Almighty?
7.asv: Canst thou by searching find out God? Canst thou find out the Almighty unto perfection?

8.web: They are high as heaven. What can you do? They are deeper than Sheol. What can you know?
8.asv: It is high as heaven; what canst thou do? Deeper than Sheol; what canst thou know?

9.web: Its measure is longer than the earth, and broader than the sea.
9.asv: The measure thereof is longer than the earth, And broader than the sea.

10.web: If he passes by, or confines, or convenes a court, then who can oppose him?
10.asv: If he pass through, and shut up, And call unto judgment, then who can hinder him?

11.web: For he knows false men. He sees iniquity also, even though he doesn’t consider it.
11.asv: For he knoweth false men: He seeth iniquity also, even though he consider it not.

12.web: An empty-headed man becomes wise when a man is born as a wild donkey’s colt.
12.asv: But vain man is void of understanding, Yea, man is born as a wild ass’s colt.

13.web: “If you set your heart aright, stretch out your hands toward him.
13.asv: If thou set thy heart aright, And stretch out thy hands toward him;

14.web: If iniquity is in your hand, put it far away. Don’t let unrighteousness dwell in your tents.
14.asv: If iniquity be in thy hand, put it far away, And let not unrighteousness dwell in thy tents.

15.web: Surely then you shall lift up your face without spot; Yes, you shall be steadfast, and shall not fear:
15.asv: Surely then shalt thou lift up thy face without spot; Yea, thou shalt be stedfast, and shalt not fear:

16.web: for you shall forget your misery. You shall remember it like waters that have passed away.
16.asv: For thou shalt forget thy misery; Thou shalt remember it as waters that are passed away,

17.web: Life shall be clearer than the noonday. Though there is darkness, it shall be as the morning.
17.asv: Andthylife shall be clearer than the noonday; Though there be darkness, it shall be as the morning.

18.web: You shall be secure, because there is hope. Yes, you shall search, and shall take your rest in safety.
18.asv: And thou shalt be secure, because there is hope; Yea, thou shalt searchabout thee, and shalt take thy rest in safety.

19.web: Also you shall lie down, and no one shall make you afraid. Yes, many shall court your favor.
19.asv: Also thou shalt lie down, and none shall make thee afraid; Yea, many shall make suit unto thee.

20.web: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail. They shall have no way to flee. Their hope shall be the giving up of the spirit.”
20.asv: But the eyes of the wicked shall fail, And they shall have no way to flee; And their hope shall be the giving up of the ghost.
